title: Web Page Design

toc.title: 10.1 World Wide Web: web page, website, web browser, URL and HTML
10.2 Structure of an HTML document: html, head, title and body
10.3 Formatting tags: headings, paragraphs, line breaks, bold, italic, underline and font
10.6 Creating and viewing a small website

html:
Every website you open — the NEB results page, a news portal, the Nagarik App's web version, Wikipedia — is built from plain text files written in HTML.

A browser reads those files and turns them into headings, paragraphs, pictures, tables and links.

In this lesson you learn how the World Wide Web works and then write web pages yourself: the structure of an HTML document, tags for formatting text, lists, images, links and tables, and finally a small website of linked pages that you can open in any browser.

All the code in this lesson was tested in a real browser (Chromium), and what it shows is described exactly.

What questions on this lesson ask

Expect the full forms WWW, HTML, URL, HTTP(S); definitions of web page, website, home page, web browser, tag, attribute; the parts of a URL; the four structure tags; the difference between container and empty tags; and writing HTML code for a given output — headings, a formatted paragraph, an ordered or unordered list, an image, a hyperlink, or a table (often with rowspan or colspan).

You will also be asked what a given code shows in the browser. Practise writing code by hand, with every tag closed.

10.1 World Wide Web: web page, website, web browser, URL and HTML

The World Wide Web (WWW, or "the web") was invented by Tim Berners-Lee, a British scientist at CERN, the European physics laboratory near Geneva.

He proposed it in March 1989, wrote the first web server, the first browser and HTML by the end of 1990, and announced the web to the public in August 1991.

In 1993 CERN made the web software free for everyone, and the web grew explosively.

World Wide Web

The World Wide Web is a huge collection of web pages, stored on computers called web servers all over the world and joined to one another by hyperlinks, which people open over the Internet with a web browser.

The Internet and the web are not the same. The Internet is the worldwide network of networks — cables, satellites, routers and computers joined together. The web is one service that runs on the Internet, like email, video calls and online games.

Term Meaning Example
Web page a single document on the web, written in HTML, that can contain text, pictures, links, sound and video the results page of a school
Website a group of related web pages under one domain name, linked to each other www.neb.gov.np (National Examinations Board)
Home page the first, main page of a website, usually saved as index.html the page that opens at www.ntc.net.np
Web browser application software that requests web pages from servers and displays them Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge, Safari, Opera
Web server a computer that stores websites and sends pages to browsers when they ask the computers of a hosting company
Hyperlink text or a picture that opens another page when clicked blue, underlined words
URL Uniform Resource Locator: the unique address of a page on the web https://www.moecdc.gov.np
HTTP / HTTPS HyperText Transfer Protocol (Secure): the rules browsers and servers use to send pages; HTTPS encrypts them a padlock in the address bar means HTTPS

The parts of a URL

A domain name is read from the right. In www.janataschool.edu.np, np is the country code of Nepal, edu shows the type of organisation (education), janataschool is the organisation's own name and www is the name of its web server.

Other types used in Nepal are gov.np (government), com.np (companies) and org.np (organisations); worldwide there are .com, .org, .net and many more.

A .np domain is registered free of charge for Nepali citizens and organisations at register.com.np.

HTML

HTML

HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the language used to create web pages. It marks up text with tags that tell the browser what each part is — a heading, a paragraph, a list, a picture, a link.

HyperText means text with links to other text. HTML was created by Tim Berners-Lee; the current version is HTML5.

HTML is a markup language, not a programming language: it describes a document but cannot calculate or make decisions.

Tags. A tag is a keyword written inside angle brackets: <p>. Most tags are container (paired) tags: an opening tag <b> and a closing tag </b> with a slash, with the content between them.

A few are empty (unpaired) tags that have no content and no closing tag: <br>, <hr>, <img>. An element is the opening tag, the content and the closing tag together.

Attributes. An attribute gives extra information about an element. It is written inside the opening tag as name="value", for example <img src="school.jpg" width="300"> or <p align="center">.

HTML tags are not case-sensitive (<B> works like <b>), but lower case is the modern practice.

Container (paired) tag Empty (unpaired) tag
has an opening and a closing tag has only one tag
encloses content: <b>bold</b> has no content: <br>
e.g. <html>, <p>, <h1>, <a>, <table> e.g. <br>, <hr>, <img>

Tools. An HTML file is plain text, so any text editor will do: Notepad on Windows, or code editors such as Notepad++, Visual Studio Code and Sublime Text, which colour the tags. The file is saved with the extension .html (or .htm) and opened in a browser.

10.2 Structure of an HTML document: html, head, title and body

Every web page has the same skeleton:

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <title>My First Page</title>
</head>
<body>
  Namaste! This is my first web page.
</body>
</html>
Part Meaning
<!DOCTYPE html> a declaration (not a tag) telling the browser that this is an HTML5 document; always the first line
<html> … </html> the root element: everything else goes inside it
<head> … </head> information about the page — its title, character set and so on; nothing in the head appears in the window
<title> … </title> the page's title, shown on the browser tab, in bookmarks and in search results
<body> … </body> everything that appears in the browser window: text, pictures, lists, tables, links

Nesting. Elements fit inside one another like boxes, and they must be closed in the reverse order of opening: <b><i>Nepal</i></b> is correct, <b><i>Nepal</b></i> is not.

Indenting the code (as above) makes the nesting easy to see.

The body tag can take attributes for the whole page, for example <body bgcolor="lightyellow" text="navy"> for the background and text colours.

Like <font> and align below, these old attributes still work in browsers but are replaced in HTML5 by CSS (styles), which you will meet in Grade 9.

Worked example 10.1 — your first web page

Problem. Write, save and open a web page whose tab reads My First Page and whose window shows Namaste! This is my first web page.

Solution.

  1. Open Notepad and type the seven lines of code shown above.
  2. File → Save As. Choose a folder, e.g. D:\mysite. In Save as type choose All files (*.*), type the name first.html, keep Encoding: UTF-8, and click Save.
  3. Double-click first.html in File Explorer; it opens in the default browser. The tab shows My First Page and the window shows Namaste! This is my first web page.
  4. To change the page, edit it in Notepad, save (Ctrl + S) and press F5 in the browser to reload. Ctrl + U in the browser shows the page's source code.
"first.html.txt" is not a web page

If Save as type is left as Text Documents (*.txt), Notepad saves first.html.txt, which opens as plain text in Notepad again.

Always choose All files and type the .html extension yourself — and switch on File name extensions in File Explorer so you can see what you saved.

The browser ignores extra spaces and line breaks in the code: three spaces show as one, and pressing Enter in Notepad does not start a new line on the page. Lines and paragraphs are made with tags.

Notes for yourself can be written as comments, <!-- like this -->, which the browser does not show.

10.3 Formatting tags: headings, paragraphs, line breaks, bold, italic, underline and font

Tag Purpose Example
<h1> … <h6> headings, <h1> the largest and most important, <h6> the smallest; shown bold with space above and below <h1>Nepal</h1>
<p> a paragraph, with a blank line above and below <p>Text…</p>
<br> a line break: the next text starts on a new line (empty tag) Kathmandu<br>Nepal
<hr> a horizontal rule (line) across the page (empty tag) <hr>
<b> bold text (<strong> also bolds, marking important text) <b>China</b>
<i> italic text (<em> also italicises, for emphasis) <i>India</i>
<u> underlined text <u>Everest</u>
<sup> / <sub> superscript / subscript x<sup>2</sup>, H<sub>2</sub>O
<font> font face, size (1–7, default 3) and colour of text <font face="Arial" size="5" color="green">

The align attribute of headings and paragraphs takes left (default), center, right or justify: <h1 align="center">. Colours are written as names (red, green, navy) or as hexadecimal codes such as #FF0000 (red) and #008000 (green).

Worked example 10.2 — formatting text

Problem. Write the HTML for a page titled Nepal that shows a main heading Nepal, a sub-heading Geography, a paragraph in which China is bold and India is italic, a paragraph in which Mount Everest is underlined and the height starts on a new line, a horizontal line, and the words Visit Nepal! in green Arial at size 5.

Solution.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <title>Nepal</title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Nepal</h1>
  <h2>Geography</h2>
  <p>Nepal lies between <b>China</b> and <i>India</i>.</p>
  <p>Its highest peak is <u>Mount Everest</u>,<br>8,848.86 metres high.</p>
  <hr>
  <p><font face="Arial" size="5" color="green">Visit Nepal!</font></p>
</body>
</html>

The browser shows the two headings in bold, <h1> larger than <h2>; the paragraphs with China in bold and India in italics; Mount Everest underlined, with 8,848.86 metres high. starting on the next line because of <br>; a grey line across the page from <hr>; and Visit Nepal! in larger green Arial letters.

`<font>` and `align` are old HTML

The <font> tag and the align, bgcolor and text attributes come from older HTML.

Browsers still obey them, and they are in your syllabus, but HTML5 replaces them with CSS: the same green text is written <p style="color: green; font-family: Arial; font-size: 24px;">Visit Nepal!</p>.

Learn the old tags for the exam and know that CSS is the modern way.

10.4 Lists, images and hyperlinks

Lists

Unordered list <ul> — items marked with bullets. Each item is an <li> (list item). The type attribute chooses the bullet: disc (filled circle, the default), circle (hollow) or square.

Ordered list <ol> — items numbered automatically. type chooses the numbering: 1 (1, 2, 3 — default), A (A, B, C), a (a, b, c), I (I, II, III) or i (i, ii, iii); start chooses the first number.

Lists can be nested: a <ul> or <ol> placed inside an <li> makes sub-points. A description list <dl> holds terms <dt> and their descriptions <dd>.

Worked example 10.3 — what the browser shows

Problem. What does the browser show for this body?

<h3>Fruits of Nepal</h3>
<ul type="square">
  <li>Mango</li>
  <li>Litchi</li>
  <li>Orange</li>
</ul>
<h3>Making tea</h3>
<ol>
  <li>Boil water.</li>
  <li>Add tea leaves.</li>
  <li>Add milk and sugar.</li>
</ol>
<ol type="I" start="3">
  <li>Kathmandu</li>
  <li>Pokhara</li>
  <li>Chitwan</li>
</ol>

Solution. The heading Fruits of Nepal, then Mango, Litchi and Orange each with a small square bullet; the heading Making tea, then the steps numbered 1. 2. 3.; then Kathmandu, Pokhara and Chitwan numbered III. IV. V. — Roman numerals (type="I") starting from 3 (start="3").

Images

The empty tag <img> places a picture on the page:

<img src="images/school.jpg" alt="Our school building" width="320">
Attribute Meaning
src source: the file name or path of the picture (required)
alt alternative text: shown if the picture cannot load, and read aloud for blind users
width, height size in pixels (give only one to keep the shape)
border a border around the picture, in pixels (old HTML)
align left or right: the picture floats and text flows beside it (old HTML)

Pictures for the web are usually JPG (photos), PNG (drawings, logos, transparency) or GIF (simple animations). The path is relative to the page: images/school.jpg means "the file school.jpg in the folder images, next to this page".

Hyperlinks

The anchor tag <a> makes a hyperlink; its href (hypertext reference) attribute gives the destination, and the text between the tags is what the visitor clicks. Links appear blue and underlined, and purple once visited.

Kind of link Code
to another website (external) <a href="https://www.welcomenepal.com">Nepal Tourism Board</a>
to another page of the same site <a href="about.html">About us</a>
to open an email message <a href="mailto:info@janataschool.edu.np">Email us</a>
to open in a new tab <a href="https://www.neb.gov.np" target="_blank">NEB</a>
a picture as a link <a href="gallery.html"><img src="images/trip.jpg" alt="Photos"></a>
to a place on the same page <a href="#notices">Notices</a> jumps to <h2 id="notices">
Worked example 10.4 — a picture and links

Problem. A page in the same folder as an images folder has this body. The file missing.jpg does not exist. What does the browser show?

<h2>Phewa Lake</h2>
<img src="images/pokhara.jpg" alt="Phewa Lake, Pokhara" width="300">
<img src="images/missing.jpg" alt="Photo of Phewa Lake (file missing)" width="200">
<p>Read more at the <a href="https://www.welcomenepal.com">Nepal Tourism Board</a> website.</p>
<p><a href="about.html">About us</a> | <a href="mailto:info@janataschool.edu.np">Email us</a></p>

Solution. The heading, then the first picture 300 pixels wide. For the second picture the browser finds no file, so it shows a small broken-picture icon with the alt text Photo of Phewa Lake (file missing) — the reason alt matters.

Then a paragraph in which Nepal Tourism Board is a blue underlined link to that website, and a line with two links: About us opens about.html, and Email us opens the email program with the address filled in.

10.5 Tables in HTML

A table is built row by row:

Tag Meaning
<table> … </table> the whole table
<caption> a title, shown centred above the table
<tr> a table row
<th> a table heading cell — bold and centred
<td> a table data cell — normal and left-aligned
Attribute Used in Effect
border="1" <table> draws lines around cells (without it the table has no lines)
cellpadding="6" <table> space inside each cell, between text and border
cellspacing="2" <table> space between neighbouring cells
width, bgcolor, align <table>, <td> width, background colour, position
colspan="2" <th>, <td> the cell spans two columns
rowspan="2" <th>, <td> the cell spans two rows
Worked example 10.5 — two tables

Problem.(a) Write the code for a bordered table captioned Class 8 Results with headings Name, Maths and Science and two rows: Asha 85 92 and Rohan 72 64.(b) What does the following code show, and how many cells does it have?

<table border="1" cellpadding="6">
  <tr>
    <th rowspan="2">Day</th>
    <th colspan="2">Periods</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th>1st</th>
    <th>2nd</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Sunday</td>
    <td>Maths</td>
    <td>Science</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Monday</td>
    <td colspan="2">Sports Day</td>
  </tr>
</table>

Solution. (a)

<table border="1">
  <caption>Class 8 Results</caption>
  <tr>
    <th>Name</th>
    <th>Maths</th>
    <th>Science</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Asha</td>
    <td>85</td>
    <td>92</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Rohan</td>
    <td>72</td>
    <td>64</td>
  </tr>
</table>

The caption appears centred above; the three headings are bold and centred.

(b) A 4-row, 3-column routine: Day fills two rows on the left, Periods fills two columns above 1st and 2nd, the Sunday row has three cells, and Sports Day stretches across both period columns on Monday.

Counting the <th> and <td> tags: 2 + 2 + 3 + 2 = 9 cells, filling the 4 × 3 = 12 places because three cells each cover two places (12 − 3 = 9).

Every row must add up

In a table, every row must cover the same number of columns once the spans are counted. If the first row has colspan="2" plus one cell (3 columns), every other row must also total 3. A missing <td> or an extra one makes the columns slip out of line.

10.6 Creating and viewing a small website

A website is a set of web pages in one folder, linked to each other by a menu of links. Plan it on paper first: the pages, what each holds, and the links between them (a site map).

Steps

  1. Make a folder mysite, and inside it a folder images holding the pictures (e.g. school.jpg).
  2. Write the home page and save it in mysite as index.html:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <title>Shree Janata School - Home</title>
</head>
<body bgcolor="#f2f7ff">
  <p>
    <a href="index.html">Home</a> |
    <a href="about.html">About</a> |
    <a href="gallery.html">Gallery</a> |
    <a href="contact.html">Contact</a>
  </p>
  <hr>
  <h1 align="center">Shree Janata Secondary School</h1>
  <p align="center"><i>Lakeside, Pokhara</i></p>
  <img src="images/school.jpg" alt="Our school building" width="320">
  <h2>Notices</h2>
  <ul>
    <li>Science Exhibition on 15 Falgun</li>
    <li>Admission open for Grade 6</li>
  </ul>
</body>
</html>
  1. Save a copy as about.html, keep the head and the menu, change the title to Shree Janata School - About and replace the rest of the body with that page's content. Do the same for gallery.html and contact.html, so every page has the same menu.
  2. View: double-click index.html. Tested in Chromium, it shows a pale blue page with the menu of four blue links, a line, the centred heading and the italic address, the picture and the bulleted notices; clicking About opens about.html and the tab changes to Shree Janata School - About.
  3. Test every link and picture, in more than one browser if you can, and fix any page that does not work.
  4. Publish (optional): to put the site on the Internet, copy the folder to a web server through a hosting service, and connect a domain name to it. Free hosting such as GitHub Pages exists, and a .np domain is free for Nepali citizens and organisations.
Worked example 10.6 — find the mistakes

Problem. A student's page shows a broken picture; clicking About us gives "File not found"; the second paragraph comes out bold as well; and the word Pokhara does not appear at all.

The files in the folder are index.html, about.html and images/logo.png. Find the four mistakes:

<img src="image/logo.png" alt="School logo">
<a href="About.htm">About us</a>
<p>Welcome to <b>our school.</p>
<p>We teach Grades 1 to 10.</p>
<p align="center>Pokhara</p>

Solution. (1) The folder is images, not image: write src="images/logo.png". (2) The file is about.html, not About.htm: the extension is wrong, and on web servers capital letters matter too, so write href="about.html".

(3) <b> is never closed, so the browser keeps the bold going into the next paragraph: write <b>our school.</b>.

(4) The quotation mark after center is missing, so the browser reads everything up to the next quotation mark as the attribute's value and Pokhara disappears: write align="center".

Activity 10.1 — your own three-page website

Make a folder named after your district. Write three pages — index.html (home), places.html and contact.html — with the same menu of links on each.

The home page needs a heading, a paragraph with bold and italic words, and a picture; places.html needs an ordered list of five places and a table of their distances from your school; contact.html needs an email link.

Test every link in two browsers, then show your teacher the code with Ctrl + U.

Writing HTML in the exam

Always start with the skeleton: <!DOCTYPE html>, <html>, <head> with <title>, <body>. Close every container tag in reverse order, put attribute values in double quotes, and indent nested tags.

For a table, draw the grid first and count the cells of every row, including the spans.

Chapter summary

  • The WWW (Tim Berners-Lee, CERN, 1989–1991) is a collection of linked web pages on web servers, opened over the Internet with a browser. A web page is one HTML document; a website is related pages under one domain; the home page is index.html.
  • URL (Uniform Resource Locator) = protocol (https://) + domain name (www.name.edu.np) + path + file name. HTTP(S) is the transfer protocol.
  • HTML (HyperText Markup Language, now HTML5) uses tags in angle brackets: container tags <p>…</p>, empty tags <br>, <hr>, <img>; attributes go in the opening tag: name="value".
  • Structure: <!DOCTYPE html>, <html>, <head> with <title> (shown on the tab), <body> (shown in the window). Close tags in reverse order.
  • Formatting: <h1>–<h6>, <p>, <br>, <hr>, <b>, <i>, <u>, <sup>, <sub>, <font face size color> (old; CSS today), align.
  • Lists: <ul type="disc|circle|square">, <ol type="1|A|a|I|i" start="n">, <li>. Image: <img src alt width height>. Link: <a href="…">, mailto:, target="_blank".
  • Tables: <table border>, <caption>, <tr>, <th> (bold, centred), <td>; colspan, rowspan. A website is a folder of linked pages with the same menu, saved as .html and tested in a browser.

Practice questions

Answers to Group A

1. (b) — Tim Berners-Lee at CERN, 1989–1991.

2. (a) — HyperText Markup Language.

3. (b) — Edge is a browser; Notepad is a text editor.

4. (b) — https is the protocol and results.html the file name.

5. (c) — <br> has no closing tag.

6. (b) — the title is shown on the tab.

7. (c) — <h1> is the largest.

8. (b) — capital letters starting from the 2nd, B.

9. (c) — src (source); alt is the alternative text.

10. (a) — the anchor tag with href.

11. (b) — colspan spans columns.

12. (c) — .html (or .htm).

Group B — Short answer (2 marks each)

  1. Differentiate between a web page and a website. [2]
  2. What is a URL? Name its parts in https://www.moecdc.gov.np/index.html. [2]
  3. Differentiate between the Internet and the World Wide Web. [2]
  4. Differentiate between container and empty tags with two examples of each. [2]
  5. What is an attribute? Give an example. [2]
  6. Write the basic structure of an HTML document. [2]
  7. Write HTML code to show Computer Science as the largest, centred heading and Grade 8 below it in red. [2]
  8. Write the code for an unordered list of three districts with square bullets. [2]
  9. Write the code to insert the picture rhino.jpg, 250 pixels wide, with suitable alternative text. [2]
  10. Write code that makes the words Visit NEB a link to https://www.neb.gov.np, opening in a new tab. [2]
Answers to Group B

1. A web page is a single HTML document that can be viewed in a browser. A website is a collection of related web pages under one domain name, linked together, such as www.neb.gov.np.

2. A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is the unique address of a resource on the web. Parts: protocol https://, domain name www.moecdc.gov.np, file name index.html.

3. The Internet is the worldwide network of networks — the cables, routers and computers. The World Wide Web is a service that runs on the Internet: the collection of linked web pages opened with a browser. (Email is another Internet service.)

4. A container tag has an opening and a closing tag around content, e.g. <p>…</p>, <b>…</b>. An empty tag has no content and no closing tag, e.g. <br>, <hr>, <img>.

5. An attribute gives extra information about an element and is written in the opening tag as name="value", e.g. <img src="logo.png"> or <p align="center">.

6.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <title>Page title</title>
</head>
<body>
  Page content
</body>
</html>

7.

<h1 align="center">Computer Science</h1>
<p><font color="red">Grade 8</font></p>

8.

<ul type="square">
  <li>Kaski</li>
  <li>Chitwan</li>
  <li>Jhapa</li>
</ul>

9. <img src="rhino.jpg" alt="One-horned rhinoceros" width="250">

10. <a href="https://www.neb.gov.np" target="_blank">Visit NEB</a>

Group C — Long answer (4 marks each)

  1. Write the HTML for a page titled My District that shows a centred main heading, a paragraph with one bold and one italic word, a line, and a numbered list of three places to visit. [4]
  2. Write the HTML for this table, with a border and the caption Marks: a header row Name, English, Nepali; and rows Sita 78 85 and Hari 66 72. [4]
  3. Write the HTML for a table whose first row is a heading Fee Details spanning three columns, followed by the heading row Grade, Monthly fee, Exam fee and the rows 7, 1500, 300 and 8, 1700, 350. How many cells does it have? [3+1]
  4. Explain the steps to create a two-page website (home and about) linked to each other, and to view it in a browser. [4]
  5. Explain the terms web browser, URL, HTML and hyperlink with one example each. [4]
Answers to Group C

1.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <title>My District</title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1 align="center">Kaski District</h1>
  <p>Kaski is famous for <b>Phewa Lake</b> and the <i>Annapurna</i> range.</p>
  <hr>
  <ol>
    <li>Sarangkot</li>
    <li>World Peace Pagoda</li>
    <li>Davis Falls</li>
  </ol>
</body>
</html>

2.

<table border="1">
  <caption>Marks</caption>
  <tr>
    <th>Name</th>
    <th>English</th>
    <th>Nepali</th>

Model answer D1: the web and the structure of an HTML document (10 marks)

Introduction. The World Wide Web (WWW) is a huge collection of linked web pages stored on servers all over the world and reached through the internet. It was invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989–1990 (Plate 10.H).

  1. Web page: one document of the web written in HTML, which may have text, pictures, audio, video and links.
  2. Website: a collection of related web pages under one domain name, such as a school's website. The first page is the home page.
  3. Web browser: the software that fetches and shows web pages: Chrome, Firefox, Edge and Safari.
  4. URL (Uniform Resource Locator): the address of a page, for example https://www.example.com.np/about.html. It has the protocol (https), the domain name (www.example.com.np) and the page or file name (about.html).
  5. HTML (HyperText Markup Language): the language of web pages. It uses tags in angle brackets to tell the browser how to show the content. Most tags come in pairs, an opening tag <b> and a closing tag </b>.

Structure of an HTML document.

<html>
  <head>
    <title>My School</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    <h1>Welcome to Our School</h1>
    <p>This is my first web page.</p>
  </body>
</html>
Tag Meaning
<html> Holds the whole document
<head> Information about the page, not shown in the page area
<title> The name shown on the browser tab
<body> Everything that the visitor sees

Steps to make a page. Open Notepad, type the code, save it as index.html with the type All Files, and double-click the file; it opens in the browser.

Conclusion. An HTML page is plain text with tags; the head holds the title and the body holds the content, and the browser turns the tags into the page we see.

Model answer D2: HTML tags and a small web page (10 marks)

Introduction. HTML tags format the text, make lists, put in pictures, link to other pages and build tables. The tags below are grouped by their use.

Purpose Tag Example
Headings (largest to smallest) <h1> to <h6> <h2>Our Class</h2>
Paragraph <p> <p>Hello</p>
Line break (no closing tag) <br> Line one<br>Line two
Bold, italic, underline <b>, <i>, <u> <b>Important</b>
Font <font> <font color="red">Red</font>
Unordered list <ul> and <li> bullets
Ordered list <ol> and <li> numbers
Image <img src=""> <img src="school.jpg" width="200">
Link <a href=""> <a href="page2.html">Next</a>
Table <table>, <tr>, <th>, <td> rows and cells

A small web page.

<html>
  <head><title>Class 8 Page</title></head>
  <body>
    <h1>Class 8 Computer Science</h1>
    <p>Our <b>subjects</b> are:</p>
    <ol>
      <li>Nepali</li>
      <li>English</li>
      <li>Computer Science</li>
    </ol>
    <img src="class.jpg" width="200">
    <table border="1">
      <tr><th>Name</th><th>Roll</th></tr>
      <tr><td>Asha</td><td>1</td></tr>
      <tr><td>Bikash</td><td>2</td></tr>
    </table>
    <a href="contact.html">Contact us</a>
  </body>
</html>

How it appears. A large heading, a paragraph with the word subjects in bold, a numbered list of three subjects, a picture 200 pixels wide, a table with a border and two data rows, and a clickable link to the page contact.html.

Points to remember.

  1. <tr> makes a row, <th> a bold heading cell and <td> a data cell.
  2. src tells the picture's file; href tells the link's target.
  3. Keep the image in the same folder as the page, or give its full path.
  4. Every opened tag must be closed, except tags such as <br> and <img>.

Conclusion. With only a few tags we can build a complete page with a heading, text, a list, a picture, a table and a link, and we see the result by opening the file in a browser.
